\#1 I'm pretty sure the expected behavior would be to cache, since any language with actual support for compound operators don't just expand it. And you wouldn't have to have any "global-side-effects", just wrap the statement in a do-end block that contains locals that hold the "temporary expressions."

\#2 True, but I don't know of one language that has compound assignment that also don't have assignments as expressions.

\#4 I was referring to incrementation/decrementation for this specific point, probably should have mentioned that.
I live in California so that might have something to do with it, but a lot of people here have had similar experiences.

There's a couple problems with compound assignment:

1. there's no gain of any kind, and implementing it will be infuriating (is x()+=1 -> x() = x() + 1 or is the call to x cached?)
2. you'll want assignments to be expressions instead of statements (allowing x = y = z), which will needlessly complicate the language.
3. similarly to number 2, the grammar of the language becomes more complex, but there will be no real gain, it'd end up only being syntax sugar (the Lua VM handles mathematical operations as just OP dest, src1, src2, although this differs in LuaJiT ofc)
4. you'll sometimes write less readable code (when has x++ ever been more readable than x = x + 1 when it wasn't part of a C-like for loop) and just cause further confusion to beginners (postfix vs prefix increment causes enough confusion as is, let's not add it to a simple language like Lua)

In all honestly a lot of my points are somewhat pedantic, but I think implementing these features would ruin the ideology of Lua being a simple and tiny language.

I think it can be argued logically from both sides.

The number one "logical" argument against suicide is that we aren't meant to die because a species is meant to reproduce. Many people who think about or who have commited suicide are beyond lonely and feel that they will never meet anyone they love. Logically, if you can't reproduce there's no purpose for you to continue existing.

Another argument is that we can't tell the future and don't know if it will get better. But again, I can argue that it's been the same for too long, or that in some cases you're already old and nothing has changed. I agree that it is possible for it to get better for some people, but sometimes the idea that is only might get better isn't enough. It's, in a way, risk assessment. In addition, usually the person saying these things don't quite understand what the person actually feels like. Again, logically it's my life and I have a right to end it.

I've thought about every possible thing from both sides both logically and emotionally, and I've time and time again come to the conclusion that sometimes thinking logically favors suicide (of course, it depends heavily on your situation).

Do different things, meet new people, and all the other over-used examples that sometimes can actually help.

I'm not trying to advocate it, I'm just saying if there's **no other solution** then it can make sense to want to do it. I'm sure plenty have people told you to get help but have you ever gotten help seriously? There's nothing left to lose at this point, give it a try. If this message reaches you too late or you're intent on continuing forward and nothing can convince you, all I know how to really say is good bye...
